items.subject: VR
items.prompt: CANDID most nearly means:
items.explanation: Candid means openly saying what you really think, so honest and direct is the match; a candid friend is never secretive or polite but vague.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Hurried means done quickly and in a rush, but candid is about being open and truthful — you can be candid and take all the time you like.
why.B: Secretive means keeping things to yourself and not letting others know, which is the very opposite of being candid.
why.C: Polite but vague means softening your words until nobody can tell what you really think, while a candid person says plainly what she thinks even when it is awkward.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: THOROUGH most nearly means:
items.explanation: Thorough work covers every part of the job, so leaving nothing out fits; a thorough search is the opposite of one done in a great hurry.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Friendly to strangers says how someone treats people, while thorough says how completely something is done — every part covered, nothing skipped.
why.B: Work done in a great hurry is rushed, and rushing is how things get missed; thorough work is the opposite, covering everything carefully.
why.D: Difficult to believe describes a far-fetched story, while thorough is about how completely a job has been done, not about whether anyone believes it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: PLAUSIBLE most nearly means:
items.explanation: A plausible excuse is one that could reasonably be true, so believable is right; plausible is the opposite of impossible.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Temporary means lasting only a short time, but plausible is about whether something could reasonably be true, not about how long it lasts.
why.B: Expensive means costing a lot of money, and a plausible excuse costs nothing — it is simply one that could be true.
why.C: Impossible means it could not happen at all, which is the opposite of plausible; a plausible story is one that easily could be so.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: TEDIOUS most nearly means:
items.explanation: A tedious chore drags on and wears you out with dullness, so long and boring fits; brief and lively is its opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Hard to reach means far away or awkward to get to, like a shelf too high, whereas tedious describes a job that drags on and bores you.
why.B: Sudden and loud describes a bang or a crash, over in a moment, and a tedious job is the opposite — it drags on and on until it wears you out.
why.C: Brief and lively means short and full of energy, which is exactly what a tedious lesson is not.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: DISPUTE most nearly means:
items.explanation: To dispute a call or a claim is to argue against it and say it is not right, so to argue against is the match; someone who disputes a decision is doing the opposite of agreeing quickly.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To promise again is to give your word a second time, but disputing is about challenging what someone has said, not pledging anything.
why.C: To agree quickly is to say yes at once, and someone who disputes a decision is refusing to go along with it.
why.D: To explain politely is to make something clear in a kind way, and you can explain something you completely agree with; disputing it means saying outright that it is wrong.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: SUPERFICIAL most nearly means:
items.explanation: Superficial means staying on the surface, so a superficial cut or a superficial friendship is shallow rather than deep.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Ancient means very old, from long ago, but superficial is about depth — staying on the surface, like a superficial scratch.
why.C: Generous means giving freely to others, while superficial says how deep something goes; a superficial friendship is a shallow one, not a mean one.
why.D: Sturdy means strong and solidly built, but superficial means going no further than the surface, like a cut that barely breaks the skin.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: MEDIOCRE most nearly means:
items.explanation: Mediocre means no better than middling, so only average fits; it is the opposite of clearly excellent.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Clearly excellent means very good indeed, and mediocre falls well short of that — middling, nothing special either way.
why.B: Very expensive means costing a lot, but mediocre is about quality being middling, and something mediocre can carry any price at all.
why.D: Extremely rare means hardly ever found, while mediocre things are everywhere — the word means no better than average.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: LENIENT most nearly means:
items.explanation: A lenient teacher lets small things slide, so not strict; forgiving is the match, and strict and demanding is the opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Difficult to please describes someone you can never quite satisfy, but a lenient teacher is easily satisfied and forgives small mistakes.
why.C: Strict and demanding means holding people to every rule and expecting a lot of them, while a lenient teacher lets small slips go.
why.D: Quick to anger means losing your temper easily, whereas lenient means going easy on people, which is a calmer sort of kindness.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: ADMIRABLE most nearly means:
items.explanation: Something admirable earns real respect and praise, so worth praising fits; barely acceptable is nearly its opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Strangely old-fashioned means belonging to a much earlier time, which tells you when something comes from; admirable tells you it deserves respect.
why.B: Unusually noisy is about how much sound something makes, but admirable is about deserving praise, and the quietest acts are often the most admirable.
why.C: Barely acceptable means only just good enough to get by, and something admirable is far more than that — it earns real respect.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: SKEPTICAL most nearly means:
items.explanation: A skeptical listener is not convinced and wants proof, so doubting is right; trusting is the opposite attitude.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Sleepy means tired and ready for bed, but a skeptical listener is wide awake — she simply is not convinced yet.
why.C: Generous means quick to share what you have, while skeptical is about whether you believe something, not about what you hand out.
why.D: Trusting means taking what you are told as true without needing proof, which is the opposite of skeptical.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Even though he wanted to keep arguing, Marcus had to ______ that his sister was right.
items.explanation: To concede is to admit that someone else is right, which is what "had to" signals here; to deny or to insist that she was right would mean he never gave in.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: To insist is to keep saying firmly that you are right and refuse to back down, but the sentence says Marcus had to give in.
why.C: To imagine is to picture something in your mind, and Marcus is not picturing anything here — he actually admits his sister was right.
why.D: To deny something is to say it is not true, and denying that his sister was right is exactly what he could no longer do.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The principal stopped by our classroom to ______ the students for their hard work.
items.explanation: To commend is to praise someone for what they have done, which is what hard work earns; to scold or to warn would be the opposite reaction.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To scold is to tell someone off for doing something wrong, and hard work deserves the opposite reaction.
why.B: To warn is to tell someone about trouble that may be coming, and the students had done well, so there was nothing to warn them about.
why.D: To replace is to put something new in the place of something else, and a principal pleased with the class is not swapping the students for others.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Because her own brother was racing, Mia could not serve as a ______ judge.
items.explanation: A neutral judge favors neither side, and Mia would naturally want her brother to win; having a brother in the race would not stop her from being patient, careful, or capable.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Careful means paying close attention so as not to make mistakes, and Mia could still do that; what her brother's racing takes away is her ability to favor neither side.
why.C: Patient means waiting calmly without getting annoyed, and having a brother in the race would not make Mia impatient — it would make her want him to win.
why.D: Capable means having the skill to do the job, and nobody says Mia cannot judge, only that she could not do it fairly this time.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Ana shouted her answer before she had read the whole question — a ______ move she soon regretted.
items.explanation: Hasty means done too quickly and with too little thought, which is exactly what answering before reading is; a patient or clever move would have been the opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Clever means quick-witted and sharp, but answering before reading the whole question is the opposite of sharp, and Ana regretted it.
why.B: Patient means willing to hold back and wait without fretting, which is exactly what Ana was not — she shouted before she had finished reading.
why.D: Generous means open-handed, happy to give others what you have, and that has nothing to do with rushing an answer out too soon.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Ms. Bell wrote a helpful ______ of my essay, naming both its strengths and its weaknesses.
items.explanation: A critique is a careful judgement that weighs strong points against weak ones, which is what Ms. Bell wrote; an apology or an announcement judges nothing.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: An announcement is a public notice telling people that something is happening, but Ms. Bell was weighing up the essay, not sharing news.
why.B: An invitation asks someone to come to something, and nobody is being invited here — the writing judges the essay.
why.C: An apology says sorry for something you did wrong, and Ms. Bell had nothing to be sorry for; she was giving a judgement on the essay.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Her apology sounded ______; anyone could tell she truly meant it.
items.explanation: Sincere means truly meant, which matches the clue that she really meant it; a sarcastic apology is one that is not meant at all.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Boastful means showing off about how good you are, which is not what an apology does at all.
why.C: Sarcastic means saying the opposite of what you really mean, often to mock, so a sarcastic apology is one that is not meant — and the clue says she truly meant it.
why.D: Confusing means hard to understand, but the sentence says anyone could tell how she felt, so nothing was unclear.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Forgetting the tickets was a ______ that cost us an hour.
items.explanation: A blunder is a careless mistake, and forgetting the tickets cost the group an hour; a bargain or a reward would be something good.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A reward is something good given to you for doing well, and forgetting the tickets cost the group an hour — nobody was rewarded for that.
why.C: A bargain is something you get for less than it is worth, a piece of good luck, and losing an hour is the opposite of a good deal.
why.D: A custom is something a group has always done, a tradition handed down, while forgetting the tickets was a one-off mistake.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The judges ______ each photograph before choosing a winner.
items.explanation: To scrutinize is to examine something very closely, which is how judges pick a winner; judges who ignored the photographs could not choose at all.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Framed means set in a border ready to hang, but the judges here are choosing which photograph wins, and that means looking hard at each one.
why.B: Purchased means bought, and judges in a contest choose a winner rather than paying for the entries.
why.D: Ignored means paid no attention to, and judges who ignored the photographs could never pick a winner.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The coach said the plan had real ______ and was worth trying.
items.explanation: Merit is real worth or value, so a plan with merit is worth trying; damage, delay, and silence would all be reasons to drop it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Damage is harm done to something, which would be a reason to drop a plan rather than to call it worth trying.
why.C: Silence is the absence of sound, and a plan cannot contain silence — the coach is saying the plan has real worth.
why.D: Delay means being held up or made to wait, which would be a fault in a plan, not a reason to try it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: A ______ athlete, Nia plays goalkeeper, midfield, and forward equally well.
items.explanation: Versatile means able to do many different things well, which is what playing three positions equally well shows; clumsy and nervous name weaknesses, not range.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Clumsy means awkward, likely to trip or drop things, but playing three positions equally well is a compliment, not a complaint.
why.B: Solitary means alone or doing things by yourself, and Nia plays right across a team in three different positions.
why.D: Nervous means anxious and easily worried, and the sentence praises how much Nia can do, not how she feels before a match.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: FLAW most nearly means:
items.explanation: A flaw is a weak spot or fault, like a crack in a bowl; a reward, a journey, and a promise have nothing to do with imperfection.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A reward is what you get for doing something well, a prize or a treat, whereas a flaw is something wrong with a thing — a crack or a weak spot.
why.B: A promise is something you pledge to do, but a flaw is a fault in a thing, like a chip in a bowl.
why.D: A journey is a trip from one place to another, and a flaw has nothing to do with travelling — it is an imperfection.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: TRIVIAL most nearly means:
items.explanation: Trivial details are so small that they hardly matter, so unimportant is the match.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Expensive says how much something costs, but trivial says how much it matters, and a trivial detail is one hardly worth mentioning.
why.B: Noisy means making a lot of sound, while trivial means mattering so little that it can safely be passed over.
why.C: Frozen means turned to ice or held fast by cold, which has nothing to do with trivial, a word about small unimportant things.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: HARSH most nearly means:
items.explanation: Harsh means rough or severe, as in a harsh winter or a harsh punishment; gentle is its opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Gentle means mild and kind, the very opposite of harsh — a harsh winter or a harsh word is rough, not soft.
why.B: Curious means eager to find things out, but harsh describes something rough or severe, like a harsh punishment.
why.C: Damp means slightly wet, and although a winter can be damp, harsh means severe and hard to bear rather than merely moist.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: APPROVE most nearly means:
items.explanation: To approve something is to judge it good and agree to it, so to accept as good fits; to argue against it is the opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To argue against something is to speak out and say it is wrong, which is the opposite of approving it.
why.B: To forget entirely is to let something slip out of your mind, but approving is an active decision that something is good.
why.D: To repeat aloud is to say something over again, and you could repeat a plan aloud without approving of it at all.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: PRUDENT most nearly means:
items.explanation: A prudent choice is a careful, sensible one that avoids needless risk, so careful and wise is right; bold and reckless is its opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Loud and talkative describes how much noise a person makes, but prudent is about thinking ahead, and a quiet person and a chatty one can both be prudent.
why.C: Rich and famous is about money and being well known, while prudent describes how carefully someone thinks before acting.
why.D: Bold and reckless means rushing in without weighing the risk, which is the opposite of prudent.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: SHODDY most nearly means:
items.explanation: Shoddy goods are put together cheaply and badly, so poorly made fits; carefully built is the opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Expensive means costing a lot of money, and something shoddy is usually cheap rather than costly; shoddy is about how badly a thing is made, not its price.
why.B: Brightly colored means having strong, vivid colors; shoddy is about the quality of the work, and a badly made thing can be any color at all.
why.D: Carefully built means put together with attention so that it lasts, which is the exact opposite of shoddy.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: FLATTER most nearly means:
items.explanation: To flatter is to pile on more praise than is deserved, often to get something; to blame unfairly is the opposite kind of remark.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: To blame unfairly is to accuse someone of a fault that is not theirs, whereas to flatter is the opposite kind of remark: praise laid on thicker than the person has earned.
why.C: To arrive early is to turn up before the time set; flatter has nothing to do with time, and means to praise someone more than they deserve.
why.D: To explain clearly is to make something easy to understand; to flatter is to praise someone far beyond what is deserved, often to get something out of them.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: CONDEMN most nearly means:
items.explanation: To condemn something is to declare that it is very wrong, so to strongly disapprove is the match; praising and celebrating point the other way.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To celebrate loudly is to make a noisy show of joy over something good, while to condemn is to declare that something is very wrong — the two point in opposite directions.
why.C: To praise quietly is still to say good things about something; condemning is declaring it wrong, which is the reverse.
why.D: To repair something carefully is to mend what is broken, but to condemn is to say in words that something is very wrong, which mends nothing.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Ravi tends to ______ when he tells the story, so the fish he caught grows another foot longer every time.
items.explanation: To exaggerate is to make something sound bigger than it really was, which is why the fish keeps growing with every telling.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: To apologize is to say sorry for something you did, and Ravi is not saying sorry — he is making the fish bigger with every telling.
why.C: To whisper is to speak very softly; the trouble with Ravi is not how loudly he tells the story but that he makes it bigger than it really was.
why.D: To hesitate is to pause because you are not sure, and Ravi never pauses — he simply adds another foot to the fish.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: We were told not to ______ about our victory, no matter how proud we felt.
items.explanation: To boast is to brag about your own success, exactly what proud winners were warned against; complaining and grumbling are what a losing team might do.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: To grumble is to complain in a low, muttering way, which is what an unhappy person does; these winners were proud, so the warning was about bragging.
why.C: To chatter is to talk quickly and lightly about small things, but the warning here is about crowing over a win, which is bragging rather than idle talk.
why.D: To complain is to say out loud that you are unhappy about something; a proud winning team has nothing to complain of, which is why they were warned about bragging instead.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Their plan was ______; one hard question and it fell apart.
items.explanation: Flimsy means weak and easily broken, so a plan that collapses at the first hard question is flimsy; sturdy is its opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Lengthy means long, going on and on; a plan can be long and still collapse, so length is not what failed here — weakness is.
why.B: Generous means willing to give freely, which describes a person's kindness rather than whether a plan can stand up to one hard question.
why.C: Sturdy means strong and solidly made, and this plan fell apart at the first hard question, so it was the opposite of sturdy.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Before repairs began, an expert came to ______ the damage.
items.explanation: To assess damage is to judge how bad it is before deciding what to do; an expert would not be sent for to ignore or enjoy it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To enjoy something is to take pleasure in it, and nobody sends for an expert to take pleasure in damage — they send for someone to judge how bad it is.
why.B: To cause something is to make it happen, but the damage had already happened before the expert arrived, so his job was to judge it, not create it.
why.C: To ignore something is to take no notice of it on purpose; an expert called in before repairs begin is there to look closely, not to look away.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Her excuse was ______: she had a doctor's note for that morning.
items.explanation: A valid excuse is one that really holds up, and a doctor's note is solid proof; untrue would mean the opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Hilarious means extremely funny, and a doctor's note is what makes an excuse hold up — nothing about it is a joke.
why.C: Untrue means false, and the doctor's note is exactly what shows her excuse was genuine, so untrue is the opposite of what the sentence tells you.
why.D: Hidden means put out of sight, and she produced a doctor's note, so her excuse was shown openly rather than concealed.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Spending his whole allowance on one poster now seems ______ to Theo, who has nothing left for the class trip.
items.explanation: Foolish means showing poor judgement, and Theo can now see that the poster was a bad use of his money; a wise choice would have left him enough for the trip.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Generous means giving freely to other people; Theo spent the money on a poster for himself, and the point is that it left him short, not that he gave anything away.
why.C: Wise means showing good judgement, and Theo now has nothing left for the class trip, so his choice turned out to be the opposite of good judgement.
why.D: Cheerful means happy and in good spirits; Theo may well feel gloomy, but the word here has to describe his decision, not his mood.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The ______ shopper compared prices at three stores before buying.
items.explanation: A shrewd shopper judges value cleverly, which is why she checked three stores first; a careless shopper would have taken the first price offered.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Generous means ready to give away what you have, which is a fine quality but not the one on show here: comparing prices at three stores is judging value sharply.
why.B: Sleepy means drowsy and ready for bed, and a shopper who visits three stores before buying is wide awake and thinking hard.
why.C: Careless means not paying attention, but this shopper paid a great deal of attention, checking three stores before she spent her money.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: After years of service, the librarian was ______ of the town's highest honor.
items.explanation: To be worthy of an honor is to deserve it, and years of service is exactly what earns one.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Jealous means wanting what somebody else has, or fearing you will lose what is yours; the librarian is the one being given the honor, so there is nobody for her to envy.
why.C: Guilty means having done something wrong, and years of service is the opposite — it is what earns an honor rather than what deserves blame.
why.D: Afraid means frightened; the sentence is about deserving the town's highest honor, not about being scared of it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The young pianist won wide ______ after her first concert.
items.explanation: Acclaim is loud public praise, the natural result of a successful first concert; blame would follow a failure instead.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Silence is the absence of sound or of comment, and a successful first concert wins loud public praise, which is the opposite of nobody saying anything.
why.B: Confusion means being muddled and not understanding, but her concert was a success, and what a success earns is public praise rather than puzzlement.
why.D: Blame is being held responsible for something that went wrong, which follows a failure; this pianist's first concert was a triumph.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: BENEVOLENT most nearly means:
items.explanation: Bene means “good,” and a benevolent neighbour wishes other people well, so kind and generous is the match; being strict about rules is a different quality entirely.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Strict about rules means insisting that every rule be kept exactly, which is a different quality from benevolent — bene means "good", and a benevolent person wishes others well, strictly or not.
why.C: Noisy and restless describes someone who cannot sit still or stay quiet, while benevolent is about wishing other people well, and a quiet person can be just as kind.
why.D: Quick to forget things means forgetful, having a poor memory; benevolent is about goodwill toward other people, not about what you can remember.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: MALICIOUS most nearly means:
items.explanation: The prefix mal- means “bad,” so a malicious rumour is spread on purpose to hurt someone — meaning to do harm.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Extremely tired is what exhausted means, but malicious comes from mal-, "bad", and describes someone who means to do harm, however rested that person is.
why.C: Difficult to lift means heavy, and malicious describes an intention to hurt somebody, which has no weight at all.
why.D: Brightly colored means full of strong, vivid colors; malicious is not about how a thing looks at all, but about meaning to do harm on purpose.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: DEJECTED most nearly means:
items.explanation: De- means “down” and ject means “thrown,” so a dejected player walks off the field thrown down — low in spirits.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Highly organized means keeping everything tidy and in order, but dejected is a feeling — de- means "down" and ject means "thrown", so it means low in spirits.
why.B: Very wealthy means having a great deal of money, while dejected describes spirits thrown down, which happens to rich and poor alike.
why.C: Wide awake means alert and not at all sleepy, and you can be wide awake and downhearted at the same moment.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: ABRUPT most nearly means:
items.explanation: An abrupt stop or an abrupt answer comes with no warning at all, so sudden fits; lengthy is closer to its opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Colorful means full of bright colors, or lively and vivid, and abrupt is about something happening with no warning, which has nothing to do with how it looks.
why.B: Polite means having good manners, and an abrupt answer is close to the opposite — so short and unexpected that it can seem rude.
why.C: Lengthy means long and drawn out, which is the opposite of abrupt: begun or finished all at once, with no warning.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: OBSTRUCT most nearly means:
items.explanation: Ob- means “against” and struct means “build,” so to obstruct a road is to put something in the way — to block it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To polish is to rub something until it shines, whereas obstruct is built from ob- "against" and struct "build", so it means putting something in the way.
why.B: To measure is to find out how big or how long something is, but to obstruct a road is to put something across it so that nothing can get past.
why.D: To invite is to ask somebody to come, and to obstruct is the reverse — standing in the way so that nothing can come through.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: RETRACT most nearly means:
items.explanation: Re- means “back” and tract means “pull,” so a cat retracts its claws and a writer retracts a statement — both take back.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To write down is to put words on paper, whereas retract is re- "back" and tract "pull", so a writer who retracts a statement pulls it back after it has already been written.
why.C: To shout loudly is to say something at great volume, but retracting is about withdrawing what you said, not about how loudly you said it.
why.D: To repeat often is to say the same thing again and again, which is the opposite of retracting it — pulling it back in, the way a cat pulls in its claws.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: CREDIBLE most nearly means:
items.explanation: The root cred means “believe,” as in credit and incredible, so a credible witness is a believable one.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Costly means expensive, and credit may be what makes you think of money, but the root cred means "believe", so a credible witness is one you can believe.
why.B: Recent means happening not long ago, while credible is about whether an account can be believed, and an old account can be every bit as believable as a new one.
why.C: Crowded means full of people, and credible describes a witness or a story you can believe, which is not a matter of numbers.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: NOVICE most nearly means:
items.explanation: Nov- means “new,” so a novice is someone new to an activity — a beginner, whatever else she may also be.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A volunteer is somebody who offers to help without being paid, and a novice may well be a volunteer too, but nov- means "new", so the word itself says only that she is new to the thing.
why.C: A leader is the one who guides everybody else, and nov- means "new", so a novice stands at the other end — new to the activity and still learning it.
why.D: A stranger is somebody you do not know, but a novice may be perfectly familiar to you and still be new at the activity, which is all the word claims.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: SURPLUS most nearly means:
items.explanation: Sur- means “over,” so a surplus is what is left over once everyone has enough — an extra amount, the exact opposite of a shortage of supplies.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A serious mistake is a bad error, and surplus comes from sur- "over", meaning what is left over, which is not a mistake at all.
why.B: A short delay is a little wait before something happens, but a surplus is about amount rather than time — it is what remains once everyone has enough.
why.D: A shortage of supplies is having too little of something, and a surplus is exactly the reverse: more than is needed.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: VERDICT most nearly means:
items.explanation: Ver- means “truth” and dict means “speak,” so a verdict is what the jury speaks at the end of a trial; the speeches and the stories all come before it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A lawyer's long speech is an address to the court arguing one side, and the verdict is ver- "truth" and dict "speak" — what the jury speaks once all the speeches are done.
why.C: A written promise is a contract or pledge set down on paper, whereas a verdict is spoken aloud at the end of a trial to settle the matter.
why.D: A witness's story is testimony, an account of what that person saw, and it is evidence heard before the verdict rather than the verdict itself.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The team watched the little robot ______ and waited for its lights to reappear.
items.explanation: Sub- means “under,” so to submerge is to go down under the water, which is why the crew has to wait for the lights to come back into view.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To assemble is to put the parts of something together, or to gather in one place, but this robot is already built — the crew is waiting for lights that have sunk out of sight beneath the water.
why.B: To announce is to make something known out loud, but the robot is doing something rather than saying something, and lights that have to reappear tell you it has gone down under the water.
why.C: To apologize is to say sorry, and a robot has nothing to be sorry for; the crew waiting for its lights to reappear tells you it has gone down under the water.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The bats slept in a cool ______ chamber the cavers reached only after an hour’s climb down.
items.explanation: Sub- means “under” and terra means “earth,” so a subterranean chamber lies underground at the bottom of a long climb; bats would not sleep in a flooded one.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Transparent means clear enough to see straight through, like glass, and this chamber is described by how far down it lies, not by what you can see through it.
why.B: Portable means easy to carry from place to place, and a stone chamber an hour's climb below ground is the last thing anybody could pick up and carry.
why.D: Flooded means filled or covered with water, and although caves can flood, this chamber is simply a cool one deep underground, where the bats can sleep dry.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Announcing the winner before the last runner had finished turned out to be ______: the trophy had to be handed to someone else.
items.explanation: Pre- means “before,” so something premature happens too early; the announcement was clearly not harmless, since the trophy had to change hands.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Impossible means it could not happen at all, but the announcement plainly did happen — the trouble was that it happened too early.
why.C: Harmless means doing no damage, and this announcement did do damage, since the trophy had to be taken back and handed to somebody else.
why.D: Traditional means done a certain way for many years because that is the custom, and there is nothing customary about naming a winner before the race has finished.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: It is rude to ______ your grandmother in front of guests, even when you are sure she is wrong.
items.explanation: Contra- means “against” and dict means “speak,” so to contradict is to speak against what someone has just said — which is what makes it rude here.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Imitate means to copy the way someone speaks or moves; the clue "even when you are sure she is wrong" is about arguing with what she said, not about copying her.
why.B: Praise means to say out loud how good someone is, which is a kind thing to do in front of guests, not the rude thing the sentence needs.
why.D: Congratulate means to tell someone you are glad about their success or good luck, and nobody would call that rude.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The ______ of a whole week at the beach kept the twins cheerful all through exam season.
items.explanation: Pro- means “forward” and spect means “look,” so a prospect is something you look forward to; a penalty or a disappointment would not keep anyone cheerful.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A penalty is a punishment for breaking a rule, and a punishment waiting for you would not keep anyone cheerful through exam season.
why.B: A disappointment is the flat feeling you get when something you hoped for does not happen, but the twins are cheerful precisely because the beach week is still ahead of them.
why.C: A burden is a heavy load that weighs you down, and a week at the beach is the opposite of a weight on your shoulders.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Because the harvest was so large, the country was able to ______ tons of rice to its neighbors.
items.explanation: Ex- means “out” and port means “carry,” so to export rice is to carry it out of the country to buyers elsewhere.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Postpone means to put something off until later, but the large harvest let the country send its rice to its neighbors, not delay anything.
why.C: Memorize means to learn something by heart so you can say it without looking, and you cannot memorize tons of rice.
why.D: Inherit means to receive money or property from someone after they die, which is not how a country sends its harvest abroad.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The jeweler offered to ______ our initials on the inside of the ring.
items.explanation: Scrib and script mean “write,” so to inscribe initials on a ring is to write or carve them into it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Rehearse means to practice a play, a speech, or a piece of music before performing it, and the jeweler is not practicing anything — he is cutting initials into the ring.
why.C: Predict means to say what will happen before it happens, and the jeweler is putting initials on the ring rather than foretelling anything.
why.D: Swallow means to send food or drink down your throat, which has nothing to do with marking initials inside a ring.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Workers set out barrels to ______ traffic around the flooded street.
items.explanation: Di- means “aside” and vert means “turn,” so to divert traffic is to turn it aside — here, around the flooded street.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Flatten means to press or knock something flat, and the barrels are there to send the cars a different way, not to squash them.
why.B: Applaud means to clap to show you like something, and traffic at a flooded street needs steering, not applause.
why.D: Purchase means to buy, and the workers are steering traffic around the flood, not paying for it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: One strong kick was enough to ______ the swimmer all the way to the far wall.
items.explanation: Pro- means “forward” and pel means “drive,” so to propel the swimmer is to drive her forward to the far wall.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Forgive means to stop being angry with someone for what they did, which is not something a kick can do to a swimmer.
why.B: Dissolve means to break up and spread right through a liquid until it disappears, the way sugar does in water, and a swimmer crossing a pool does no such thing.
why.D: Measure means to find out how big or how far something is, but the kick did not find out the distance — it drove her along it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Ms. Reyes asked Dev to speak up, because his answer was barely ______ at the back of the room.
items.explanation: Aud means “hear” and -ible means “able to be,” so audible means able to be heard — which is why Dev is asked to speak up.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Edible means safe to eat; it ends in -ible just as audible does, but edible is about food while audible is about what can be heard.
why.B: Grateful means thankful, which tells you how Dev feels rather than whether the back of the room could hear him.
why.C: Portable means able to be carried about easily, like a portable radio, but Ms. Reyes is asking about how well Dev can be heard.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: EJECT most nearly means:
items.explanation: E- means “out” and ject means “throw,” so to eject is to throw or force something out — the opposite of joining it together.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To measure carefully is to find out exactly how big or how much something is, while eject is about throwing something out, not sizing it up.
why.B: To join together is to fasten two things into one, which is the reverse of eject, where the e- means out.
why.D: To praise loudly is to say aloud how good someone is, and eject has nothing to do with approval — only with forcing something out.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: SPECTACLE most nearly means:
items.explanation: Spect means “look,” so a spectacle is something people stop to look at — a remarkable sight, not a sound.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A long journey is a trip from one place to another, but spect means look, so a spectacle is something worth stopping to look at, wherever you are.
why.B: A quiet whisper is speech so soft you can barely hear it, and a spectacle is something you see rather than something you hear.
why.C: A small mistake is something done wrong, while a spectacle is a sight that makes people stare.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: MANUSCRIPT most nearly means:
items.explanation: Manu means “hand” and script means “write,” so a manuscript is the author’s own written text, before any printing happens.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A musical instrument is something you play, like a violin or a flute; manu means hand and script means write, so a manuscript is writing, not music.
why.C: A printed poster is made by a machine and pasted up for everyone to read, whereas a manuscript is the author's own text as she wrote it, before any printing.
why.D: A spoken speech is words said aloud to an audience, but script means write, so a manuscript sits on the page rather than in the air.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: RUPTURE most nearly means:
items.explanation: Rupt means “break,” as in erupt and interrupt, so a rupture in a pipe is a break in it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A loud cheer is a shout of approval from a crowd, which is only noise; a rupture is something breaking, as in erupt and interrupt.
why.C: A warm welcome is the friendly greeting you give someone who arrives, while a rupture is something splitting or breaking apart.
why.D: A long delay means being kept waiting, which is about time, but a rupture is about something breaking, like a burst pipe.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: AVERT most nearly means:
items.explanation: A- means “away” and vert means “turn,” so you avert your eyes by turning them away.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: To sing along is to join in with the words of a song, which is something you do with your voice, while a- means away and vert means turn, so averting your eyes is turning them away.
why.C: To count again is to go back over a total to check it, and avert has nothing to do with numbers — it means turning away.
why.D: To gather up is to collect things together into one place, which brings them toward you, while avert turns something away.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: MAGNITUDE most nearly means:
items.explanation: Magn- means “great,” as in magnify, so the magnitude of an earthquake is how great it is.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A bad habit is something you do over and over without thinking about it, while magn- means great, so magnitude is about how great something is.
why.B: A soft sound is a faint one, but magnitude does not name a sound at all — it names how great a thing is, like the magnitude of an earthquake.
why.D: A short pause is a brief stop, which is about time, whereas magnitude is about size.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: FLUENT most nearly means:
items.explanation: Flu means “flow,” as in fluid, so fluent speech flows easily; the word is about talking, not about running, lifting, or drawing.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Being able to run very fast makes you swift or speedy; flu means flow, and it is a fluent speaker's words that flow, not her feet.
why.B: Being able to lift heavy loads makes you strong, while fluent describes words coming out smoothly, not muscles.
why.C: Being able to draw neatly makes you a careful artist, but fluent is about speech that flows easily, not about a steady hand.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: VACANT most nearly means:
items.explanation: Vac means “empty,” as in vacuum and vacate, so a vacant seat has nobody in it — the opposite of crowded.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Crowded means packed full of people, which is the opposite of vacant — vac means empty, as in vacuum.
why.C: Expensive means costing a lot of money, but a vacant room is simply an empty one, and an empty room can be cheap or costly.
why.D: Noisy means full of sound, while vacant is about whether anyone is there at all, and an empty hall is usually the quiet one.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: She had forgotten to mention the party, so she squeezed it into a ______ after she had already signed her name.
items.explanation: Post- means “after” and script means “write,” so a postscript is added after the letter is finished and signed; a preface would come first instead.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A preface is the short introduction at the front of a book, before the main text, so a preface comes first while she added her note after signing.
why.B: A caption is the line of words printed under a picture to explain it, not something you squeeze onto the end of a letter.
why.C: A heading is the title at the top of a page or section, so it goes first, but she remembered the party only after she had signed her name.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The dentist used a small tool to ______ the loose tooth.
items.explanation: Ex- means “out” and tract means “pull,” so to extract the loose tooth is to pull it out.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Assemble means to fit parts together to build something, which is the reverse of what the dentist does in pulling a tooth out.
why.C: Translate means to put what someone said or wrote into another language, and the tooth is being pulled, not put into words.
why.D: Inflate means to fill something with air until it swells, like a balloon, while the dentist is drawing the tooth out rather than pumping it up.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The whale rose to the surface to ______ a spray of air and water.
items.explanation: Ex- means “out” and pel means “drive,” so to expel the spray is to drive it out of the blowhole.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Borrow means to take something for a while meaning to give it back, and the whale is pushing the spray out, not taking anything.
why.B: Gather means to collect things together and bring them in, whereas the whale is driving the spray out of its blowhole.
why.D: Invent means to make something that never existed before, but air and water already exist and the whale is simply blowing them out.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The radio tower can ______ a signal for a hundred miles.
items.explanation: Trans- means “across” and mit means “send,” so the tower sends a signal across a hundred miles.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Sharpen means to give something a fine point or edge, the way you sharpen a pencil, and a tower is not putting a point on its signal.
why.C: Decorate means to make something look prettier by adding things to it, which is not what a radio tower does with a signal.
why.D: Swallow means to send food or drink down your throat, which if anything is the opposite of sending a signal out across a hundred miles.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The hospital needed a ______ receptionist, because half the families who came in spoke only Spanish.
items.explanation: Bi- means “two” and lingua means “language,” so a bilingual receptionist can speak with the Spanish-speaking families as well as the English-speaking ones; being punctual or courteous would not solve that problem.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Courteous means polite and well mannered, and however polite the receptionist is, politeness alone will not let her understand a family speaking Spanish.
why.C: Punctual means always on time, which is a fine quality but no help when half the families speak a language the receptionist does not.
why.D: Reliable means you can count on someone to do what she promised, but the receptionist could turn up faithfully every day and still not understand the families who speak only Spanish.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The sign warns drivers to stop for any ______ in the crosswalk.
items.explanation: Ped means “foot,” so a pedestrian is a person travelling on foot — exactly who a crosswalk is meant for.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A delivery truck is a vehicle that brings goods to people's doors, but ped means foot, and a crosswalk is painted for people crossing on foot.
why.B: A chimney is the tall shaft above a fireplace that lets smoke out through the roof, and no chimney ever stood in a crosswalk.
why.C: A textbook is a book you study a subject from, so it is not something a sign would tell drivers to stop for.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The Romans built a stone ______ across the valley, and the city’s fountains ran for the first time.
items.explanation: Aqua means “water” and duct means “lead,” so an aqueduct leads water into the city, which is why the fountains could finally run.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: An archway is a curved opening you walk or ride through, and although an aqueduct is often carried on rows of arches, an archway by itself brings no water to the fountains.
why.C: A monument is a statue or structure built to keep the memory of a person or an event alive, and admiring one would never make the fountains run.
why.D: A furnace is a closed chamber where a fire burns to heat a building or melt metal, so it gives the city heat rather than the water it needed.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: A single lantern was enough to ______ the whole tent.
items.explanation: Lumin means “light,” as in luminous, so to illuminate the tent is to light it up.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Flatten means to press or squash something flat, which is not what a lantern does to a tent.
why.C: Translate means to put words into another language, and a lantern gives light, not words.
why.D: Purchase means to buy, so a lantern can be purchased but it cannot purchase anything itself.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Her second jump was so long that it seemed to ______ the school record.
items.explanation: Sur- means “above,” so to surpass the school record is to go beyond it — her jump was longer than the old best.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Postpone means to put something off until later, but her jump had already happened, and what it did was go beyond the old record.
why.B: Borrow means to take something for a while meaning to return it, and a record is not lent out — it is beaten.
why.D: Describe means to say in words what something is like, and the jump did not talk about the record, it went past it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: FRUGAL most nearly means:
items.explanation: Frugal describes someone who spends carefully and avoids waste, so wasting money is its opposite; being frugal says nothing about how much money a person was born with or about giving it away.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Being eager to give money away is being generous, while frugal describes someone careful about what she spends, which is a different quality altogether.
why.B: Being born into great wealth is about how much money you start with, but frugal is about how carefully you spend it, and rich and poor people alike can be frugal.
why.C: Being quick to waste money is the exact opposite of frugal, since a frugal person spends carefully and tries never to waste anything.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: INQUISITIVE most nearly means:
items.explanation: An inquisitive person asks questions and wants to find things out; fear, boasting, and refusing to change are different traits altogether.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Being quick to boast about winning is showing off after a victory; an inquisitive person is not showing anything off, she is asking questions because she wants to find things out.
why.C: Being unwilling to change plans is stubbornness, keeping to what you already decided; inquisitive is about wanting to know more, which has nothing to do with plans.
why.D: Being frightened by new places is fear of the unfamiliar, and an inquisitive person feels the opposite about anything new — she wants to go and find out about it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: ARROGANT most nearly means:
items.explanation: Arrogant means having too high an opinion of yourself — the opposite of shy, and unrelated to forgiving or to being careful.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Being shy around strangers means feeling small and quiet with people you do not know, which is the reverse of arrogant — an arrogant person thinks very highly of herself.
why.B: Being quick to forgive means letting a wrong go easily; arrogant is about how high an opinion you hold of yourself, which is a different thing altogether.
why.C: Being careful with details means checking the small things closely; arrogant describes a swollen opinion of yourself, and a careful person need not have one.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: STERN most nearly means:
items.explanation: A stern teacher looks and sounds serious and expects the rules to be kept; gentleness, cheerfulness, and hesitation all point the other way.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Gentle and forgiving means soft with people and quick to let a fault go, and a stern teacher is the opposite — she means the rule to be kept.
why.C: Unsure and hesitant describes someone holding back because she does not know what to do; a stern person is not hesitating at all, she is being firm.
why.D: Cheerful and chatty means bright and full of talk, and stern is the grave, serious face that makes a room go quiet.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: DILIGENT most nearly means:
items.explanation: A diligent worker keeps at a job carefully and steadily, so giving up quickly and working carelessly are its opposites; sharing is a different trait.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Careless in a hurry means rushing and letting mistakes through; diligent means the opposite, working steadily and taking the care the job needs.
why.C: Quick to give up means dropping a task as soon as it gets hard, and a diligent worker is exactly the one who stays with it.
why.D: Unwilling to share is about holding on to what is yours; diligent describes how hard and steadily you work, which is a different thing entirely.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: EARNEST most nearly means:
items.explanation: Earnest means you truly mean what you say and say it seriously, which rules out joking, rudeness, and boredom.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Joking and playful means treating things lightly, for fun; earnest is the opposite — an earnest person means every word she says.
why.B: Bored and distant describes someone whose mind has drifted away, and an earnest person is the one who cares most about what is being said.
why.C: Angry and rude is about a hot temper and bad manners; earnest says only that you are serious and truly mean it, and you can be earnest quite politely.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: INDIGNANT most nearly means:
items.explanation: Indignant is the particular anger you feel when something is unjust. Delight, curiosity, and worry are not anger at all.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Delighted means filled with pleasure, and indignant is anger — the particular anger you feel when something is unfair.
why.C: Curious means wanting to find out about something; indignant is not a question at all, it is anger at unfairness.
why.D: Worried means uneasy about what might happen next, and indignant is not unease at all — it is the anger you feel when something is unfair.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: ENVIOUS most nearly means:
items.explanation: An envious person looks at what someone else has and wishes it were hers, so being glad about another's good luck is the opposite feeling; fear and pride are different feelings altogether.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Being afraid of new people is shyness, and envious is not fear at all — it is wanting what somebody else has.
why.B: Being glad about other people's good luck is the very opposite of envious; an envious person wishes that luck had been hers instead.
why.D: Being proud of your own success is about what you have done yourself, and envious is about looking at what somebody else has and wanting it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: ENTHUSIASTIC most nearly means:
items.explanation: An enthusiastic helper throws herself into the job because she is genuinely excited about it, which rules out boredom, cool calm, and polite distance.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Being bored by the whole idea means it does not interest you, and enthusiastic is the opposite — brimming with interest.
why.B: Calm and very careful describes someone taking her time and weighing each step, and enthusiastic is about eagerness instead — how keen you are, not how slowly you go.
why.D: Polite but distant means being pleasant while keeping your feelings back; an enthusiastic helper holds nothing back, she throws herself in.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: CAUTIOUS most nearly means:
items.explanation: A cautious driver slows down before a blind corner, so cautious is the opposite of taking chances or rushing, and it says nothing about being friendly.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Friendly to strangers is about being warm with people you do not know; cautious is about watching for danger, and you can easily be both at once.
why.B: Willing to take chances means running the risk and hoping it turns out, which is exactly what a cautious person will not do.
why.C: Quick and impatient means rushing because waiting annoys you, and cautious means slowing down on purpose so that nothing goes wrong.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Even after his cousins offered to pay him back the next day, Marcus refused to lend a single dollar, and the family found his ______ behavior hard to forgive.
items.explanation: “Hard to forgive” marks the word as criticism, and refusing a loan that would be repaid the next day costs him nothing — so the praising words thrifty, frugal, and practical (all meaning wise with money) cannot fit; only stingy, which means mean about giving, does.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Frugal means careful and sparing with money, and it is praise; the family is not praising Marcus, and refusing a loan he would have back the next day saves him nothing.
why.B: Practical means sensible and down-to-earth about how things really work, and there is nothing sensible about refusing to lend a dollar the cousins would have handed straight back.
why.C: Thrifty is praise too — it means making your money go a long way by not wasting it, and nothing here was going to be wasted, since the cousins would have paid him back.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Nobody saw who took the last cupcake, but the ______ grin Rico wore when the empty plate was found told everyone exactly who had.
items.explanation: The grin that gives him away shows he got the cupcake by quiet trickery, which is what sly means; honest is the opposite, gracious describes warm manners, and someone who is puzzled has not just pulled off a trick.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Honest means truthful and open, but Rico is hiding what he did and the grin gives him away; sly means getting something by quiet trickery.
why.C: Puzzled means not understanding something, and Rico understands perfectly well what became of the cupcake — that is why he is grinning.
why.D: Gracious means warm and well-mannered, and Rico's grin is not good manners; it is the look of someone pleased with a trick he has got away with.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The inventor's claims were ______: she said the new battery might last an hour longer, not that it would change the world.
items.explanation: Claiming only an extra hour rather than changing the world keeps her claims small and unexaggerated, which is what modest means here; boastful and grand describe exactly the big claims she avoids, and her careful wording is the opposite of reckless.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Reckless means charging ahead without thinking what could go wrong, and the inventor is doing the careful opposite — claiming only what she is sure of.
why.B: Boastful means talking up how good you are, and the inventor does the reverse — she deliberately keeps her claim small.
why.C: A grand claim is a huge, sweeping one, and hers was deliberately small — one extra hour, not changing the world.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: When the rest of the team stopped speaking to Priya after the missed penalty, Dana walked home with her as she always had; nobody who knew Dana was surprised at how ______ she was.
items.explanation: Standing by a friend when everyone else turns away is faithfulness, which is what loyal means; the sentence is not about bragging, about being liked by the crowd, or about running out of patience.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Popular means liked by a great many people, and the sentence is not about how many people like Dana — it is about her standing by the one friend everyone else dropped.
why.C: Boastful means going on about how good you are, and Dana says nothing about herself; she just keeps walking Priya home.
why.D: Impatient means quickly annoyed at having to wait; nobody is waiting for anything here, and walking Priya home is faithfulness, not irritation.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: His advice was accurate but so ______ that it stung: “Your essay is dull, and you never checked the spelling.”
items.explanation: “Stung” rules out gentle and tactful, and the quoted remark names two specific faults, which rules out vague; blunt means honest in a way that spares no feelings.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Gentle means soft and careful of people's feelings, and his advice stung, so it was anything but gentle; blunt means saying the truth without softening it.
why.B: Vague means unclear and short on detail, and he named two exact faults — the dull writing and the unchecked spelling — so his advice was the opposite of vague.
why.C: Tactful means telling the truth in a way that spares the other person's feelings, and his remark spared none, which is what made it sting.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Nobody had asked Mr. Odile to drive two hours with the costumes the cast had forgotten, and the cast was so ______ that they made him a card and clapped when he walked in.
items.explanation: Making a card and clapping for someone who drove two hours unasked is a show of thanks, which is what grateful means; annoyance and indifference would show no thanks at all, and nothing about the drive puzzles them.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Puzzled means confused and unable to work something out; nothing confuses the cast here — they know exactly what Mr. Odile did and are thanking him for it.
why.B: Indifferent means not caring one way or the other, and a card and applause are what people do when they care very much.
why.D: Annoyed means mildly cross, and the cast has nothing to be cross about — the forgotten costumes were their own fault and he put it right.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The assembly opened with a ______ minute of silence for the school's founder, and even the youngest students stopped fidgeting.
items.explanation: A minute of silence that makes small children go still is grave and dignified, which rules out festive, playful, and casual.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Playful means full of fun and games, and this is the moment even the fidgeters go still; solemn means grave and serious.
why.C: Casual means easy-going and informal, the way you are with friends, and a minute of silence for the school's founder is as formal as an assembly gets.
why.D: Festive means cheerful in the way a party or a holiday is, and this silence is a mark of respect, which is grave rather than merry.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Ms. Ortiz did not excuse the late homework, but her voice was so ______ that Danny came away feeling understood rather than scolded.
items.explanation: “Feeling understood rather than scolded” rules out severe and mocking, and indifference would leave him feeling nothing; sympathetic means sharing in how someone else feels.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Indifferent means not caring either way, and an indifferent voice would have left Danny feeling nothing at all rather than understood.
why.B: Severe means harsh and stern; Ms. Ortiz did hold him to the rule, but she did it in a kind voice, and severe describes a voice that is not kind.
why.C: Mocking means making fun of someone, and nobody is laughing at Danny — he comes away feeling understood.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The box of old camp photographs left Grandma smiling and ______, saying again and again how much she missed those summers by the lake.
items.explanation: She is smiling and speaking fondly of what she misses, which rules out bitter and anxious; nothing is being waited for, so not impatient. Nostalgic is exactly this fond longing for the past.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Impatient means fed up with waiting, and Grandma is not waiting for anything; she is looking back at summers that are already over.
why.C: Anxious means worried about what might happen, and her feeling points backwards to the lake summers she misses, not forwards to anything to fear.
why.D: Bitter means sour and angry over something that went wrong, and she is smiling as she remembers, so her feeling is fond rather than sour.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: By the last mile of the hike Ana had stopped chattering altogether, and her answers came out in a ______ mumble.
items.explanation: Falling silent and mumbling at the end of a long hike shows worn-out tiredness, which is what weary means; a cheerful or playful hiker would still be talking, and nothing on the trail has alarmed her.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Cheerful means bright and in good spirits, and Ana has gone quiet and is mumbling, which is what being worn out looks like at the end of a long walk.
why.C: Playful means in the mood for fun and games, and someone in that mood would still be chattering; Ana has stopped altogether.
why.D: Alarmed means suddenly frightened by something, and nothing on the trail has frightened Ana — she is simply worn out.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: BOASTFUL most nearly means:
items.explanation: A boastful person keeps announcing how good he is; complaining, fear, and generosity are unrelated traits.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Always complaining about others is grumbling and faultfinding, and a boastful person's subject is not other people at all — it is himself.
why.C: Being very generous with money means giving it away freely, and boastful says nothing about money; it is about how a person talks about himself.
why.D: Being easily frightened by noise is being jumpy or timid, and a boastful person is not shrinking from anything — he is announcing how good he is.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: GRACIOUS most nearly means:
items.explanation: Gracious describes warm good manners, the direct opposite of coldly rude, and it has nothing to do with confusion or humor.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Wildly funny is about making people laugh, which is humor rather than manners, and gracious is about how warmly and politely you treat people.
why.B: Being confused by simple things means struggling to understand, and gracious has nothing to do with how quickly you understand — it is about kind good manners.
why.D: Coldly rude is meeting someone with no warmth at all, and gracious is its exact opposite — warmth and good manners.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: RESENTFUL most nearly means:
items.explanation: Resentful is the sour anger left behind by treatment you think was unfair; gratitude is its opposite, and eagerness and puzzlement are not anger.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Being eager to begin a task is keenness, wanting to get started, while resentful is a sour, angry feeling that looks back at something already done to you.
why.C: Grateful means thankful for a kindness, and resentful is its opposite — the bitterness left behind when you feel you were treated unfairly.
why.D: Being puzzled by a new rule means not understanding it, and a resentful person understands the rule perfectly well — she just feels she was treated unfairly and stays angry about it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: MELANCHOLY most nearly means:
items.explanation: Melancholy is a low, lingering sadness, so humor, energy, and alertness all miss it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Extremely funny is about making people laugh, and melancholy is a low, lingering sadness — the furthest thing from laughter.
why.C: Wide awake is about being alert rather than sleepy, and melancholy describes a mood; you can feel melancholy wide awake or half asleep.
why.D: Full of energy describes someone bursting to get going, and melancholy is a quiet, heavy sadness that slows a person down.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: GRIM most nearly means:
items.explanation: Grim describes something stern and cheerless; hopeful, silly, and welcoming are all the opposite in feeling.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Warm and welcoming is how a friend greets you at the door, and grim is the opposite — hard, cheerless and forbidding.
why.B: Silly and light means playful and not serious, while grim is heavy and severe, the look on a face when the news is bad.
why.C: Bright and hopeful means expecting things to turn out well, and grim is the opposite in feeling — hard, cheerless and gloomy to look at.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: APOLOGETIC most nearly means:
items.explanation: Apologetic means showing that you regret something you did; pride, anger, and curiosity carry no regret.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Being proud of a win is pleasure in something you did well, and apologetic is the opposite feeling — regret for something you did badly.
why.C: Being curious about a plan means wanting to know more about it, and apologetic carries no question in it at all, only sorriness for a fault.
why.D: Being angry at a rule is temper aimed at the rule, and an apologetic person is not angry; she is admitting she was in the wrong.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: SCORNFUL most nearly means:
items.explanation: Scorn is contempt, so scornful means treating something as beneath you — the opposite of admiring, and unrelated to helpfulness or uncertainty.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Eager to help describes someone quick to pitch in, which says nothing about scorn — scorn is the cold feeling that a thing is beneath you.
why.C: Admiration is looking up to someone and thinking well of them, which is the exact opposite of scorn — a scornful person looks down.
why.D: Being unsure of the answer is doubt, which is about not knowing something; scorn is about looking down on a thing as not worth your respect.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: DEFIANT most nearly means:
items.explanation: Defiant means openly standing against an order, the opposite of obedient; amusement and gratitude are different feelings entirely.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Easily amused means quick to find things funny, which is about laughing, not about standing up to an order.
why.B: Grateful means full of thanks for something you have been given, and someone defiant is refusing rather than thanking.
why.D: Quietly obedient means doing as you are told without any fuss, which is the very opposite of defiant — defiance is refusing out loud.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Though the whole town praised her invention, Maya stayed ______, insisting that her science teacher deserved as much credit as she did.
items.explanation: She insists on sharing the credit, which rules out smug, and insisting aloud is not timid; she plainly cares, so not indifferent. Humble means not thinking too highly of yourself.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Timid means shy and easily frightened, but Maya insists out loud that her teacher deserves the credit, and insisting takes nerve rather than shyness.
why.C: Indifferent means not caring one way or the other, and Maya plainly cares a great deal — she insists her teacher be given credit.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: After the win, Trent's grin was ______, and he reminded everyone yet again that he had predicted the score exactly.
items.explanation: Reminding everyone “yet again” of his own correct prediction is self-satisfied, not gracious; he is neither sorry (apologetic) nor worried (anxious) after winning.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Gracious means being kind and generous about other people, especially when you have won, and Trent does the opposite by reminding everyone of his own cleverness.
why.D: Apologetic means looking sorry, as though you wished you had not done something, and Trent is enjoying himself far too much for that.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The kitten's ______ streak showed the moment she batted every pencil off the desk and darted away with her tail high.
items.explanation: Knocking pencils down harms nobody, so vicious (cruel) is far too strong; she is causing trouble, so not obedient, and darting off tail-high is not timid. Mischievous means playfully naughty.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Obedient means doing what you are told, and a kitten who sweeps every pencil off the desk is doing the opposite of what she is told.
why.B: Vicious means cruel and meaning to cause harm, which is far too strong for a kitten knocking pencils about for fun.
why.D: Timid means shy and easily scared, but this kitten darts off with her tail high, which is the swagger of a confident cat.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Two goals behind at half time, Coach stayed ______, telling the players the comeback was still theirs for the taking.
items.explanation: He encourages the team, which rules out gloomy and furious, and “still theirs for the taking” shows he is sure rather than uncertain; optimistic means expecting things to turn out well.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Gloomy means low-spirited and expecting the worst, and the coach tells his players the comeback is still theirs, which is expecting the best.
why.B: Furious means extremely angry, and the coach is encouraging his players rather than raging at them.
why.D: Uncertain means not knowing which way things will go, but "still theirs for the taking" is said with confidence, not with doubt.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Ravi had been certain he had failed the audition, so when the cast list went up with his name on it, he sat down on the steps looking utterly ______.
items.explanation: Seeing his name after expecting the worst lifts a weight off him, which is what relieved means; alarm, annoyance, and disappointment would all follow bad news, not good.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Disappointed is what you feel when something you hoped for does not happen, and Ravi's name is on the list, so the hoped-for thing did happen.
why.C: Alarmed means suddenly frightened by something bad, and finding out you have been cast is good news, not a fright.
why.D: Annoyed means mildly cross at something irritating, and there is nothing to be cross about when you have been cast after expecting to fail.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Rather than saying the painting was ugly, Nina gave a ______ reply, praising its colors before suggesting one change.
items.explanation: “Rather than saying it was ugly” and the praise that comes first rule out blunt and rude, and she says nothing about herself, so not boastful; tactful means honest without wounding.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Blunt means saying exactly what you think without softening it, which is precisely what Nina avoided by praising the colors first.
why.B: Boastful means showing off about yourself, and Nina says nothing about herself at all — she is talking about the painting.
why.C: Rude means openly disrespectful, and Nina goes out of her way to be kind about the painting before she suggests a change.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The old dog was ______, nudging Nora's hand until she petted him and then settling his head in her lap.
items.explanation: He seeks Nora out for petting, so he is not indifferent, and resting his head in her lap shows trust, which rules out hostile and fearful; affectionate means showing fondness.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Hostile means unfriendly and ready for a fight, and a dog who settles his head in your lap is doing the opposite of picking one.
why.C: Indifferent means not caring either way, but this dog nudges Nora's hand until she pets him, so he cares very much.
why.D: Fearful means frightened and expecting to be hurt, and a dog who feels that way shrinks back rather than pushing his head into someone's hands.

items.subject: VR
