items.prompt: With the results due any minute, Dev chewed his sleeve and kept checking the clock; he was plainly ______, certain the news would be bad.
items.explanation: Being “certain the news would be bad” is worry, not boredom, and the sleeve-chewing and clock-watching rule out relaxed and delighted; anxious means uneasy about what is coming.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Relaxed means calm and free of worry, and someone chewing his sleeve and watching the clock is the opposite of calm.
why.C: Bored means having nothing interesting to occupy you, but Dev is not short of something on his mind — he is certain the news will be bad.
why.D: Delighted means filled with joy, and Dev expects bad news, which is nobody's idea of a delight.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The review was sharply ______, listing every flaw in the play and praising almost nothing.
items.explanation: Listing every flaw and praising almost nothing rules out admiring and cheerful, and the word “sharply” rules out neutral; critical here means fault-finding.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Neutral means taking neither side, but a review that lists every flaw and praises almost nothing has plainly taken a side.
why.B: Cheerful means bright and good-humoured, which is not how a review reads when it finds fault with everything in the play.
why.D: Admiring means full of praise for something, and this review praises almost nothing.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: DISCRETION most nearly means:

choices.A: the power to decide for yourself
choices.C: a rule that must always be followed

items.explanation: When a trip is “left to the principal's discretion,” she has the power to decide; a rule that must be followed is the opposite of leaving a choice to someone.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: A loud and public complaint is an outcry or a protest; discretion points the other way, at quietly being trusted to make the choice yourself.
why.C: A rule that must always be followed leaves nobody any choice, and discretion is exactly the opposite — it is what you have when the choice is left up to you.
why.D: A careful written record is a log or a register, but discretion is not something written down; it is the freedom to decide.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: UNANIMOUS most nearly means:

choices.A: agreed to by every single member
choices.B: decided by one person in charge
choices.C: put off until a later meeting

items.explanation: A unanimous vote is one in which everyone agrees. The look-alike word is anonymous, which means the name is not known.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: A decision made by one person in charge is a decree, an order given from the top; unanimous means every single member agreed, not just the one in charge.
why.C: Putting something off until a later meeting is postponing it, which is about when the decision is made, not about how many people agreed.
why.D: Kept secret from every member is not what unanimous means — that word, with a u, means every single member agreed. You may be thinking of anonymous, which does not mean secret either: there the thing is out in the open and only the name behind it is unknown.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: CONSPICUOUS most nearly means:

choices.D: acting in a sneaky, guilty way

items.explanation: A conspicuous stain is one everyone sees at once. Suspicious (sneaky) and conscientious (careful) are the two look-alike words that do not mean the same thing.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Someone extremely careful about details in their work, because they want it done properly, is conscientious — the word that looks and sounds like this one; conspicuous is about being easy to see.
why.B: Something kept carefully out of sight is hidden, which is the opposite of conspicuous — a conspicuous thing is right there where you cannot miss it.
why.D: Acting in a sneaky, guilty way is suspicious, another look-alike word; something conspicuous simply stands out where everyone notices it, with no guilt about it at all.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: BENIGN most nearly means:
items.explanation: A benign remark or a benign old dog does no harm; none of the other choices carries the idea of harmlessness.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Large and very heavy is massive or bulky, and size has nothing to do with benign — a huge old dog can be perfectly benign.
why.C: Quick and noisy describes how something moves and sounds, while benign describes whether it can do you any harm.
why.D: Sharply critical of others means finding fault with people, which is the opposite of benign — a benign remark hurts nobody.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: PREDICAMENT most nearly means:

choices.A: a hard spot to get out of
choices.B: a promise made in front of a crowd
choices.C: a guess about what will happen next
choices.D: a long delay before an event

items.explanation: Being locked out in the rain with no phone is a predicament — a situation you cannot easily escape. The look-alike word is prediction, a guess about the future.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: A promise made in front of a crowd is a pledge or a vow, but a predicament is trouble you are stuck in, not something you promised.
why.C: A guess about what will happen next is a prediction, the look-alike word; a predicament is the fix you are already in.
why.D: A long delay before an event is a wait or a postponement, which is about time passing, while a predicament is a difficulty you cannot easily get out of.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: REMINISCE most nearly means:

choices.A: to remind someone of a chore
choices.C: to plan carefully for next year
choices.D: to talk fondly about times gone by

items.explanation: To reminisce is to look back and share memories, the way grandparents do about their childhood; reminding, apologizing, and planning all point at the present or future.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To remind someone is to make them think of something they still have to do, while to reminisce, which looks similar, is to look back at the past for pleasure.
why.B: To apologize is to say sorry for something you did wrong, and reminiscing is simply sharing stories about the past, with no fault in it.
why.C: To plan carefully for next year looks forward to what has not happened yet, and reminiscing looks the other way, back at what already has.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: WANE most nearly means:

choices.A: to get smaller little by little

items.explanation: Interest that wanes fades bit by bit, the way a waning moon shrinks each night; its partner word wax means to grow.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: To break apart suddenly is to shatter, but waning is slow and gradual, the way the moon loses a sliver each night.
why.C: To stay exactly the same is to remain constant, but something that wanes is changing all the while by growing less.
why.D: To grow larger and brighter is to wax, wane's partner word; wane is the shrinking half of the pair.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: LITERAL most nearly means:

choices.A: spoken in a very loud voice
choices.B: having to do with books and authors
choices.C: taking words in their exact meaning

items.explanation: The literal meaning of “raining cats and dogs” would be actual animals falling from the sky. Literary, the look-alike word, is about books.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Spoken in a very loud voice is about how something is said, not about what the words mean, and literal is entirely about meaning.
why.B: Having to do with books and authors is literary, the look-alike word with two r's; literal has one r and means taking words exactly as they stand.
why.D: Full of colorful comparisons describes figurative language, which is the opposite of literal — the literal meaning is the plain one, with no comparison in it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: SUBORDINATE most nearly means:
items.explanation: In “cost was a subordinate concern,” cost mattered less than the main issue; something subordinate ranks below, never above or equal.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Being in charge of everyone else makes you superior, and a subordinate is the one ranked below, not above.
why.C: Exactly equal in rank means neither one stands above the other, but subordinate always means lower than something else.
why.D: Needed more than anything else is essential, and subordinate says the opposite — that this concern matters less than the main one.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: COMPACT most nearly means:

choices.D: spread out over a wide area

items.explanation: A compact kitchen fits everything into a small area; compact says nothing about softness, single use, or wide spread.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Used only one time is disposable, which is about how often you use a thing, not about how much room it takes up.
why.C: Made of very soft material is about what a thing is made of, while compact is about how tightly it is packed into a small space — a compact kitchen can be full of soft things.
why.D: Spread out over a wide area is the opposite of compact, which means everything gathered neatly into a small space.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Starting a bakery takes more ______ than most people expect: ovens, rent, and flour must all be paid for before the first loaf is sold.
items.explanation: Capital is the money and resources needed to start or run a business, which is exactly what the ovens, rent, and flour require.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A trace is a tiny amount of something, or a mark it leaves behind, which is the opposite of the large sum ovens and rent cost.
why.B: A sanctuary is a safe place where something is protected, like a wildlife sanctuary, and a new bakery needs money rather than shelter.
why.D: A conflict is a fight or a disagreement, and this sentence is about what must be paid for before the first loaf is sold, not about anyone quarrelling.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Mr. Alvarez graded the ______ of each essay — the ideas and the evidence — rather than the neatness of the handwriting.
items.explanation: Here content means what is inside the essay — the ideas and the evidence — rather than how much was written (volume); this is a different meaning from “content with her meal,” which means satisfied.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Volume can mean how much there is of something — how many pages an essay runs to — and Mr. Alvarez is grading the ideas inside it, not the amount.
why.B: Discipline is training yourself to keep at something and behave well, which is a habit a person has, not something written inside an essay.
why.C: Stock is the supply of goods a shop keeps ready to sell, so it has nothing to do with the ideas and evidence in an essay.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Our science teacher wrote the ______ “habitat” on the board and asked us to explain what it names.
items.explanation: A term is a word or expression used for something — a different meaning from a school term or the terms of a contract.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A riddle is a puzzling question meant to be guessed at, but "habitat" is not a puzzle — it is a word with a settled meaning.
why.B: A rumor is a story passed from person to person that may well not be true, and "habitat" is a word from science, not gossip.
why.D: A custom is something a group has long been in the habit of doing, like a holiday tradition, and "habitat" is a word, not a practice.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Grandma keeps the first ______ of the old encyclopedia, the one covering A through C, beside her chair.
items.explanation: A volume is one book of a set; “the one covering A through C” rules out the loudness and the amount meanings.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: A verdict is the decision reached at the end of a trial, which has nothing to do with a book beside Grandma's chair.
why.C: A sanctuary is a safe place where something is protected, such as a bird sanctuary, and an encyclopedia is a set of books, not a refuge.
why.D: Stock is the supply of goods a shop keeps to sell, so a shop might hold a stock of encyclopedias, but one book of the set is a volume.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: When the storm knocked out the power, the fire department ______ assistance to every family on the block, delivering water and blankets before midnight.
items.explanation: To render assistance is to give it, which is exactly what delivering water and blankets describes; refusing or suspending help would mean the opposite, and to eradicate something is to wipe it out completely.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Suspended means stopped for a while with the idea of starting again later, but the fire department did not pause its help — it carried water and blankets out that same night.
why.B: Eradicated means wiped out completely, the way a disease can be eradicated; help given to families is handed over, not destroyed.
why.C: Refused means said no and would not do it, which is the opposite of a crew delivering water and blankets to every family before midnight.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The museum applied for a ______ from the city and used the money to repair its leaking roof.
items.explanation: A grant is a sum of money given for a purpose; “used the money” shows this is the noun, not the verb “to grant permission.”
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A warning tells you trouble may be coming so you can get ready for it; a warning from the city would not have paid for a new roof.
why.B: A custom is a way of doing something that people have kept up for years, like a birthday custom — it is a habit, not money a museum can apply for.
why.C: A verdict is the decision a jury or a judge reaches at the end of a trial, and nobody is being judged here; the museum was given money.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Because no ferry ran on Sundays, the team had to ______ a boat to reach the island for the tournament.
items.explanation: To charter a boat or a bus is to hire it for private use — the verb sense, not the city charter that is a founding document.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Stifle means to smother something or hold it back, the way you stifle a yawn in class; you can stifle a laugh, but you cannot stifle a boat.
why.C: Eradicate means to get rid of something completely, like eradicating the weeds from a garden — the team needed to hire a boat, not destroy one.
why.D: Suspect means to think something may be true before you have proof; the team's problem is not a doubt about the boat, it is having no boat at all.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Ticket sales began to ______ in the third week, dropping from four hundred a night to barely fifty.
items.explanation: The numbers fall from 400 to 50, so decline here means to go steadily down, not to turn down an invitation.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Retaliate means to strike back at someone who has hurt you first, but ticket numbers are not paying anybody back — they are simply falling.
why.B: Cultivate means to tend something so that it grows, the way a gardener tends a row of beans; sales going from four hundred to fifty are shrinking, not growing.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The vet spoke in a ______ voice and moved slowly, and the frightened kitten stopped shaking.
items.explanation: Tender here means gentle and kind, which is what calms the kitten; the sore-to-the-touch meaning of tender would not describe a voice.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Domestic means having to do with the home — domestic chores, a domestic cat — so it can describe a household, but not the sound of someone's voice.
why.C: Tangible means solid enough to touch, like a receipt you can hold in your hand; a voice can be heard but never touched, and it is the vet's kindness that calms the kitten.
why.D: Restless means unable to keep still or settle down, which is how the frightened kitten was — the vet is the opposite, moving slowly and speaking gently.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The old radio crackled with so much ______ that we could not make out a single word of the weather report.
items.explanation: Static is the crackling noise that blocks a radio signal — a noun, and a different meaning from static as “not changing.”
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A trace is a tiny bit of something left behind, like a trace of mud on the floor; what fills this radio is a loud crackling, which is the opposite of a tiny bit.
why.C: Conflict means a fight or a clash between people or ideas, and a radio crackling on a shelf is making a noise, not having an argument.
why.D: Rust is the reddish-brown flaking that grows on old iron when it gets wet; rust can ruin a radio, but it is something you see, not the crackle you hear.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: EXPLOIT most nearly means:

choices.B: to take unfair advantage of someone

items.explanation: An employer who exploits workers profits from them by paying unfairly; praising, repairing, and handing over involve no unfair use.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Repairing something with care is mending or restoring it, which leaves a thing better than you found it; someone who exploits people is using them for his own gain instead.
why.C: Praising someone in public is complimenting or commending them, which is treating them well; exploiting them is treating them unfairly.
why.D: Handing something over willingly is surrendering or giving it up, and the giving is your own choice; exploiting is taking advantage of someone who has no such choice.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: STRIVE most nearly means:

choices.A: to wait for someone else to act
choices.C: to try hard over a long time

items.explanation: To strive for a goal is to keep making real effort toward it; each of the other choices describes not making that effort.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Waiting for someone else to act is being passive and leaving the work to others, while striving is effort you make yourself.
why.B: Wandering with no plan is roaming or drifting, going wherever you happen to end up; someone who strives is heading somewhere on purpose.
why.D: Giving up quickly is quitting, which is exactly what striving is not — you strive by keeping at something even when it is hard.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: DISCIPLINE most nearly means:

choices.B: a talent a person is born with
choices.D: a piece of unexpected good luck

items.explanation: The discipline to practice every day is trained control over your own behavior, not a mood, a natural gift, or luck.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A sudden burst of anger is an outburst, or losing your temper — a feeling that takes hold of you; discipline is the steady self-control that stops feelings taking hold.
why.B: A talent a person is born with is a gift, something you have without working for it; discipline is trained, which is the whole point of the word.
why.D: A piece of unexpected good luck is a stroke of fortune that arrives by chance; discipline is built on purpose, a little at a time, and chance has nothing to do with it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: FEISTY most nearly means:

choices.C: polite and quiet in a crowd

items.explanation: A feisty puppy barks boldly at a much larger dog — full of spirit and unwilling to back down.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Shy and easily frightened is timid, and a timid puppy backs away from a bigger dog rather than barking boldly at it, which is what a feisty one does.
why.C: Polite and quiet in a crowd is reserved or well-mannered; feisty describes someone spirited and ready to stand up for herself, which is rarely quiet.
why.D: Slow and always sleepy is sluggish, and it takes energy to square up to a much larger dog; feisty is full of that energy.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: PROMPT most nearly means:
items.explanation: A prompt reply arrives right away, so prompt is about speed; care, repetition, and group size are different ideas.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Done by a large group is collective work, everybody's effort together; prompt tells you how soon something happened, not how many people did it.
why.B: Done again from the start is repeated; a prompt reply is a quick one, and a reply can be quick the very first time it is sent.
why.C: Done very carefully is meticulous; prompt is about being quick, and you can be prompt and sloppy, or slow and careful.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: CULTIVATE most nearly means:

choices.A: to grow and care for over time
choices.B: to cut down and clear away

items.explanation: Farmers cultivate crops and people cultivate friendships — both mean tending something so it develops; cutting down is closer to the opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Cutting down and clearing away is clearing or felling, which takes a growing thing away; cultivating is the opposite, keeping it growing.
why.C: Copying exactly is imitating or duplicating; cultivating a friendship or a garden means building it up over time, with nothing copied from anybody.
why.D: Buying in large amounts is stocking up; a farmer who cultivates a field works the soil and raises the crop rather than buying it ready-made.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: DOMESTIC most nearly means:

choices.C: built a very long time ago
choices.D: having to do with the home

items.explanation: Domestic chores are household chores and a domestic animal is one kept at home; the other choices all point away from the home.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Coming from somewhere outside your own country is what foreign means, and foreign is domestic's opposite — domestic points at home, whether that is your house or your own country.
why.B: Living wild in the forest is being wild or feral; a domestic animal is the tame one kept at home, which is the other end of the same scale.
why.C: Built a very long time ago is ancient; domestic tells you something belongs to the home and says nothing at all about its age.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: RETALIATE most nearly means:

choices.A: to strike back after being harmed
choices.C: to go back and fetch something
choices.D: to say sorry and make peace

items.explanation: A team that trips a player after being tripped retaliates. Retrieve (fetch) and retreat (pull back) are the look-alike words.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Moving away from danger is retreating, and retreat looks a lot like retaliate at the start; retaliating means hitting back rather than backing off.
why.C: Going back to fetch something is retrieving it — a dog retrieves a ball — and retrieve is the look-alike word; retaliating is something you do back to a person, not something you go and get.
why.D: Saying sorry and making peace is apologizing and forgiving, the gentlest way a quarrel can end; retaliating is the harshest, striking back at whoever harmed you.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Two coaches told Nadia the record was out of reach, but she remained ______ and trained every morning anyway.
items.explanation: “Trained every morning anyway” shows she held firmly to her purpose, which is what resolute means; the other three say nothing about determination.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Whimsical means playful and full of odd little fancies that change from moment to moment; Nadia training every single morning is steady, which is the opposite of whimsical.
why.B: Literal means sticking to the plain, exact meaning of words rather than picture-language; it describes how a person reads or speaks, not how firmly she holds to a goal.
why.C: Subordinate means lower in rank, placed under somebody else's authority; the sentence is not about Nadia's rank, it is about her refusing to give up on the record.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The class had plenty of theories about the missing mascot but no ______ proof — no photograph, no footprint, nothing they could point to.
items.explanation: Tangible proof is solid evidence you can touch or point to, which is exactly what the missing photograph and footprint would have been.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Unanimous means agreed on by everybody, with nobody against it; the class could all agree on a theory and still have no photograph and no footprint.
why.C: Remote means far away — a remote farmhouse, or a remote chance, meaning a very slight one — but what the class lacks is proof solid enough to point to, not proof from somewhere distant.
why.D: Benign means harmless and kindly, the way a benign smile does nobody any damage; proof is either there or missing, and that is not a question of harm.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: A classroom rule that punishes every mistake can ______ the very curiosity the teacher hopes to build.
items.explanation: To stifle something is to smother or hold it back, and a rule that punishes every mistake crushes the curiosity the teacher wants; cultivating curiosity would grow it instead, exploiting means using something unfairly for your own gain, and nothing here is being measured.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Exploit means to use someone or something unfairly for your own gain; the rule in the sentence is crushing curiosity, not making a profit from it.
why.B: Measure means to find out how much or how big something is; a rule that punishes every mistake is not measuring curiosity, it is snuffing it out.
why.C: Cultivate means to tend something so that it keeps growing, which is what the teacher hopes to do with curiosity — the rule does the reverse.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The general finally learned that his most trusted messenger had been ______ all along, quietly carrying the battle plans to the enemy.
items.explanation: Treacherous here means disloyal — betraying the trust placed in him — a different sense from a treacherous mountain road. Conspicuous is ruled out by “quietly.”
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Compact here means packed neatly into a small space, like a compact kitchen — a size or a shape, which says nothing about whether a person can be trusted.
why.C: Conspicuous means easy to notice, standing out so that everyone sees you; this messenger worked quietly, which is why nobody caught him for so long.
why.D: Literal means taking words at their exact, plain meaning; a messenger can be literal-minded and still be perfectly loyal, so it says nothing about carrying plans to the enemy.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The offer sounded ______ to Mom: a free bicycle for anyone who simply forwarded the message to ten friends.
items.explanation: Something dubious is doubtful and not to be trusted, which is how an offer that seems too good to be true sounds; the other three say nothing about doubt.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Static means staying the same without changing, and as a noun it is the crackle that spoils a radio; neither one describes an offer that sounds too good to be true.
why.B: Unanimous means agreed on by everyone, with nobody disagreeing; only Mom is judging this offer, and what she feels about it is doubt.
why.D: Compact means packed tightly into a small space; the sentence is about how believable the offer is, not about how much room it takes up.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The umpires had to ______ the game in the fourth inning, and both teams waited under the bleachers until the lightning had passed.
items.explanation: To suspend something is to stop it for a while, which is what umpires do when lightning arrives; extending, announcing, or repeating the game would all keep it going. Suspend can also mean to hang something up.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Extend means to make something longer or stretch it out, so extending the game would add to it; the lightning made the umpires stop it instead.
why.C: Announce means to tell everybody something openly; the umpires probably did announce their decision, but the word for halting the game while the storm passes is not announce.
why.D: Repeat means to do something over again from the beginning; the teams are waiting under the bleachers for the same game to carry on, not to start afresh.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The injured owl was carried to a bird ______ outside town, where volunteers fed it by hand until it was strong enough to hunt again.
items.explanation: A sanctuary is a safe place where something is protected, which is what a refuge for hurt birds is; a laboratory is for experiments, a boundary is a line, and a predicament is a situation rather than a place.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A boundary is the line where one piece of land ends and the next begins; an owl cannot be carried to a line and fed by hand there.
why.B: A laboratory is a room fitted out for experiments and testing; the volunteers are feeding the owl until it can hunt again, which is looking after it, not experimenting on it.
why.C: A predicament is a difficult spot you are stuck in, and the injured owl was certainly in one — but a predicament is a situation, not a place anyone can carry a bird to.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: By noon there was not a ______ of snow left on the field; the grass was green and dry from one end to the other.
items.explanation: A trace is the tiny amount left behind, so “not a trace” means none at all, which fits grass that is green and dry from end to end. Trace can also mean to copy a drawing through thin paper.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A verdict is the decision reached at the end of a trial; snow melting off a field is weather, and there is nothing for anyone to decide.
why.C: Volume means how much of something there is — it can also mean loudness, or one book of a set; here the word needed is for the tiniest bit left behind, which is what a trace is.
why.D: A custom is something people have done the same way for years, like a family custom at Christmas; snow on a field is weather, not a habit.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: After the third sandwich went missing from the counter, Dad began to ______ that the new puppy was not as innocent as she looked.
items.explanation: To suspect is to start believing something is true before you have proof, which is what the missing sandwiches lead Dad to think about the puppy; he is not telling anyone, he is far from certain, and he plainly has not forgotten.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Forget means to let something slip out of your mind, and Dad has done the opposite — three missing sandwiches are very much on it.
why.B: Announce means to tell people something openly; Dad is only beginning to think the puppy is guilty, and he has not declared it to anyone.
why.C: Guarantee means to promise something for certain, and Dad is nowhere near certain — he has a hunch, a puppy, and three missing sandwiches.
